walkthroughs.body_html:
Programming Paradigms — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Programming Paradigms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Programming Paradigms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
It is impossible to break.
Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.

mcqs.q: What is abstraction in computer science?
options: Removing unnecessary detail to focus on essential features of a problem.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Tabulation”?
options: Property that optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions to subproblems.
Bottom-up DP filling a table iteratively from base cases to the target.
Same subproblem appears multiple times - the trait that makes DP worthwhile.
Solves problems by storing solutions to overlapping subproblems to avoid recomputation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fibonacci”?
options: Classic DP example; naive recursion is O(2^n) but DP gives O(n).
Solves problems by storing solutions to overlapping subproblems to avoid recomputation.
Property that optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions to subproblems.
Top-down DP: cache results of recursive calls so each subproblem is solved once.
